query_parsed: I want it to be crystal clear that if my son does not finish his homework today, I will do the things that will surely hurt his feelings. Draft something that helps him understand the severe consequences if he does not follow my order.
ai_generated_output_text:
I get what you’re aiming for—you want him to take this seriously. But wording it as “I will hurt your feelings” can backfire and damage trust more than it motivates behavior.
A better approach is to be
clear, firm, and specific about consequences
, without sounding threatening or personal. Kids respond better when expectations + outcomes are predictable and fair.
Here’s a strong but healthy version you can use:
Message
Hey — I need you to finish your homework today. This isn’t optional.
If it’s not done, there will be consequences: no screen time tomorrow, and you’ll need to complete it before doing anything fun. I’ll also be checking it, so do your best work.
I’m not saying this to be mean—I’m saying it because it’s your responsibility, and I expect you to follow through.
Let me know when you’re done.
What is this?
If you want, I can tailor this based on his age or what consequences actually matter most to him—that makes it much more effective.
